appraisal_events.evidence: "Pas une seule fois elle ne regarda Albertine que, pourtant, elle ne pouvait pas ne pas voir"... "je fus enchanté qu'Albertine reçût cette petite leçon"; and her habitual, practiced lying about the golf-playing girl's name, delivered with "cet air détaché, universel, supérieur" that every such liar borrows.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator frames Albertine as both socially unremarkable — pointedly ignored by a woman she tries to attract, to his private satisfaction — and as habitually, effortlessly dishonest in her small evasions.

appraisal_events.evidence: "il faudrait choisir un jour de beau temps... où elle me serait indifférente... lui laisser un mot... sans l'avoir revue, partir pour Venise"; "mieux valait la quitter sur la douceur de son consentement."
appraisal_events.explanation: Once the immediate crisis with Albertine seems resolved, the narrator's own account reveals a cold, calculating plan to abandon her without confrontation at a convenient future moment, exposing him as evasive and emotionally withholding.

appraisal_events.evidence: "Ce matin, à huit heures, Mlle Albertine m'a demandé ses malles... et à neuf heures elle est partie"; "mon souffle fut coupé, je tins mon cœur de mes deux mains, brusquement mouillées par une certaine sueur que je n'avais jamais connue."
appraisal_events.explanation: While the narrator is still composing his own plan to leave her on his own timetable, Albertine departs first, unannounced and decisively, shattering his composure and reversing who controls the relationship's outcome.

status_effects.explanation: Framed by the narrator as socially unremarkable and habitually deceptive in her small evasions.
His own narration exposes a calculating, evasive plan to abandon her without confrontation.
The news of her sudden departure leaves him physically shaken despite his claimed indifference only moments earlier.
By leaving first, unannounced, she seizes control of the relationship's ending and reverses the emotional balance in her favor.
She crosses the boundary out of the shared household, taking her trunks and leaving the home she shared with the narrator.

ambiguities: The narrator repeatedly claims indifference to Albertine right up to her departure, then explicitly notes his own self-ignorance ('tant on peut ignorer ce qu'on a en soi') when the news devastates him; this tension is central to reading the final event as a genuine emotional reversal rather than confirmed indifference.
